_readme: Where every photo on the scheduled pages came from. One entry per file in public/guides/photos/: file (the path the page uses), subject, sourceUrl (the page it was taken from), originalUrl (the file downloaded), license (public-domain, CC0-1.0, CC-BY-x.x or CC-BY-SA-x.x only), credit (exactly as the source asks), downloadedOn, sha256 of the original download. scripts/validate-guide.mjs refuses a figure that is not listed here or whose licence, credit or source differ.

photos.subject: American dog tick, Dermacentor variabilis, adult female
photos.credit: CDC/DVBID/ Gary O. Maupin; photo: James Gathany (CDC Public Health Image Library, phil.cdc.gov)
photos.sourceDescription: This image depicts a dorsal view of a female, American dog tick, Dermacentor variabilis, which had been found in Panola Park near Atlanta, Georgia. D. variabilis has been found to be a vector for both Rocky Mountain spotted fever (RMSF), and tularemia.

photos.subject: Asian longhorned tick, Haemaphysalis longicornis, adult female
photos.credit: CDC/ DVBD; photo: James Gathany (CDC Public Health Image Library, phil.cdc.gov)
photos.sourceDescription: This photograph depicted a dorsal view of an adult female, Haemaphysalis longicornis   tick, commonly known as the longhorned tick. This specimen was meandering about, climbing a blade of grass. H. longicornis   ticks are able to reproduce in an asexual manner. Males are rare.
